_readme: Walks around Hollowmere (js/events/walks.js, samWalk). Placeholders depend on the section.

goddess: pre-binding disguise encounters and post-binding strolls. Placeholders: {alias}, {form}, {race}, {house}, {sam}, {goddess}. Pre-binding choices with resIn can trigger evGoddessDistract via gDistractAct (she never lets Sam finish).
casual: encounters with randomly generated NPCs (buffs Sam's Technique). Placeholders: {name}, {race}, {act}, {job}, {house}.
casualRecruit: follow-up when Sam's Technique meets walk.casual.recruitTech after a casual encounter. Placeholders: {name}, {race}, {house}.
partnerOpeners: optional custom opener lines per partner key when met on a walk; falls back to partnerDefault.

events: rest / coin / flavor walk events (type: 'rest' | 'coin' | 'flavor'). Choices declare declarative effects (energy, gold, rep, sam, appXP, mood, trust, outfit, regularLoyalty) and optional stat check (check: {stat, label, need, win, lose}).

disguise.title: A Familiar Face in the Crowd
disguise.intro:
Lanternlight catches the gold tips of long black hair three stalls ahead of you in the afternoon market. Before you can look away, {form} steps neatly out of the crowd and falls into step beside you.

"{alias}," she says brightly, linking her arm through yours as though you'd arranged to meet here. "You walk too fast, {sam}. You're going to miss everything worth looking at."
disguise.wonder:
Her palm is startlingly warm through your sleeve. You try to place her—not one of your staff, and certainly not any townswoman you remember—until she leans in close enough for you to smell faint candle smoke and warm honey.

"Looking for someone?" {alias} asks, her eyes bright with amusement.

image.comp: walking arm in arm through a sunlit market street, looking up at him with a teasing smile, hand tucked around his elbow
image.setting: busy cobblestone market street with colorful stalls and hanging paper lanterns

choices.label: "Who told you my name?"
choices.resIn: "Everyone in the Lantern Quarter talks, darling," she murmurs, backing you into the quiet alcove between two spice stalls with her palm flat over your fly. "Come here. Let me keep your hands busy so you stop thinking."
choices.res: "A little bird," she says, tapping the tip of your nose while her free hand gives your cock a bold, shameless squeeze through your trousers. By the time you blink past the scent of cinnamon and candle smoke, she has slipped into the crowd and left you aching.

choices.label: Walk with her awhile
choices.resIn: You let her lead the pace down a narrow lane behind the silk stalls. The moment nobody is looking, she pushes you against the brick and goes straight for your belt.
choices.res: You stroll the stalls with her for half an hour, trading dry remarks about the merchants while her fingers brush dangerously close to your groin every time nobody looks. When you turn to buy roasted chestnuts, the cobblestones beside you are empty.

disguise.title: At the Canal Rail
disguise.intro:
Halfway across the canal bridge, {form} is leaning over the stone parapet, watching paper boats drift beneath the arches. She glances over her shoulder as your boots hit the cobbles—black hair tipped with gold catching the late sun.

"Fancy meeting you here," {alias} purrs, patting the warm stone beside her. "Take a break. The ledger won't catch fire if you look at the river for five minutes."
disguise.wonder: You lean on the parapet beside her. Within a minute she has pressed her bare hip tight against yours, her palm sliding brazenly over your trousers to trace your growing bulge as if you weren't standing in broad daylight. Something in the effortless way she claims your space makes your pulse hammer.

image.comp: leaning against a stone canal bridge beside him, looking sideways with a sly smile, hair blowing softly in the breeze
image.setting: stone bridge over a quiet canal in warm late-afternoon light

choices.label: Ask where she's staying
choices.resIn: "Closer than you think," she whispers, steering you down into the deep shadow beneath the bridge steps with her fingers already hooking into your waistband.
choices.res: "Somewhere with a great view of {house}," she says lightly, kissing the corner of your mouth after one last slow stroke through your trousers, then slipping down the stairs before you catch your breath.

choices.label: Stay and watch the boats
choices.res: She stays until the canal lamps flicker on, resting her chin on your shoulder with one warm palm resting unrepentantly over your thighs before vanishing as a barge passes.

disguise.title: Candle Smoke at the Crossroads
disguise.intro:
A step off the main road sits an old roadside lantern shrine, mossy and quiet. Standing before the unlit brass bowl is {form}—though when she turns, you already know that gold-tipped black hair and those impossible lamp-bright eyes.

"{goddess}," you say flatly. She laughs, delighted, and snaps her fingers so the shrine wick catches with a soft pop.
disguise.wonder: "Spoilsport," she says, strolling straight up until her breasts press against your chest and her fingers hook into your belt. "Out shopping for trouble without me? Play along as {alias} if you know what's good for you—and remember the rule: you still don't get to cum."

image.comp: standing beside an old stone lantern shrine, smiling smugly with one finger brushing his collar, small ember light glowing nearby
image.setting: quiet mossy roadside shrine shaded by trees, warm dusk light

choices.label: Call her bluff and pull her behind the shrine
choices.resIn: "Oh, bold today, {sam}," {goddess} purrs, already unbuckling your trousers as she backs you behind the stone shrine.
choices.res: "Impatient," she chides softly, wrapping her fingers around your bare cock to stroke you right to the brink against the shrine stone—and vanishing in a swirl of warm candle smoke the heartbeat before you cum.

choices.label: Play along and tease her about slacking off
choices.res: "I never slack off, stranger," {alias} replies with a crooked, smug grin, pinching your ass as she walks you halfway back to {house} before fading down a side alley.

disguise.title: Out of the Rain
disguise.intro:
A sudden drizzle drives you under a narrow tavern awning, shaking water from your hoodie—only to find {form} already waiting there, completely dry despite the rain drumming on the street.

"You're soaked," {alias} notes, though her glowing gold eyes have already dropped straight to your groin. You catch that smug little smile and realize the air under the awning smells like warm wax and candle sparks.
disguise.wonder: {goddess} steps right inside your open coat, her warm palms sliding under your shirt and straight down to cup your cock through your damp trousers. "Nobody can see past the rain," she murmurs against your jaw. "So don't waste it asking dumb questions."

image.comp: standing close under a wooden awning while rain falls behind them, drying his collar with a mischievous grin
image.setting: lantern-lit cobblestone street during a light rain shower, wooden awning

choices.label: Press her against the wall and tell her to prove it
choices.resIn: "Say please, {sam}," {goddess} murmurs, parting the front of your trousers with both hands while the rain curtains off the alley behind you.
choices.res: "I wanted to remind you whose hands feel best," she whispers shamelessly, pumping your cock hard right through your fly until your hips buck—then kissing your jaw and stepping dryly into the downpour, leaving you throbbing and high and dry.

choices.label: Wait out the rain with her
choices.res: She leans shamelessly against your chest until the clouds break, drying your shirt with the heat off her bronze skin while her fingertips tap idle, teasing circles over your belt.

bound.title: Out in Disguise
bound.text:
Halfway down the market street, {form} slips smoothly into step beside you and laces her fingers through yours. You only need one glance at the gold tips of her hair and that smug sidelong grin to recognize {goddess}.

"Couldn't stand watching you stroll around town by yourself," she whispers, leaning her tits into your arm. "Come on. Buy me something sweet, pretend I'm a stranger, and let's see where you drag me afterwards."

image.comp: walking hand in hand through a busy street looking fondly at him, wearing a playful disguise
image.setting: warm afternoon market street with lanterns

choices.label: Buy her honey pastries (-20g)
choices.res: {goddess} eats both pastries with obvious delight and licks honey off her thumb just to watch you stare. "Good mortal. Wait until tonight."

choices.label: Play along with the stranger act
choices.res: You introduce yourself as if for the first time, and she plays coy all the way back to {house}—slipping her hand over your cock in every dark doorway just to make you swear.

bound.title: A Quiet Detour
bound.text: On the canal bridge, a familiar voice calls out from a bench—{goddess}, wearing {form} like a favorite coat, swinging her legs above the water. "Your ladies have the house covered for an hour," she tells you, patting the bench beside her with glowing gold eyes. "Sit. You look like you could use me."

image.comp: sitting on a stone bridge bench swinging her legs, beckoning him with an affectionate smile
image.setting: quiet canal bridge at dusk, warm lantern reflection on water

choices.label: Rest your head in her lap
choices.res: She laughs softly and cards warm fingers through your hair while your cheek rests against her bare thigh until the sky turns deep violet. You head back strangely rested.

choices.label: Tease her about sneaking out
choices.res: "Goddesses don't sneak, {sam}," she replies primly, squeezing your knee with warm fingers. "I was checking up on what's mine."

casual.title: Caught in the Rain
casual.setting: quiet cobblestone archway sheltered from a warm afternoon downpour
casual.text:
A sudden downpour chases you under a narrow stone archway—already occupied by {name}, a friendly {race} shaking rain from her hair. The two of you stand shoulder to shoulder watching the gutters flood, trading dry jokes until her gaze drops to your mouth and doesn't come back up.

"Looks like we're stuck here for a bit," she murmurs, stepping inside your coat out of the chill. "Might as well keep each other busy."
casual.goRes: Sheltered behind the archway's stone pillar, wet clothes are shoved aside fast. She gasps into your mouth while your hands work over her bare skin, and hers waste no time dropping straight to your cock until both of you are flushed, sticky, and breathless when the rain breaks.
casual.passRes: You keep your hands to yourself and chat easily until the rain slows. She waves warmly as you step back into the street.

casual.title: Upstairs at the Tavern
casual.setting: quiet sunlit upstairs room above a neighborhood tavern, narrow bed
casual.text:
At a quiet neighborhood tavern, you end up sharing a corner table with {name}, a bright-eyed {race} traveling through town. One drink turns into two, easy laughter turning warm and unhurried. When she taps her empty cup and glances toward the innkeeper's stairs, there's nothing subtle about her smile.

"My room's paid through tonight," {name} says softly, brushing your knee under the table. "Come up for an hour and show me what you've got?"
casual.goRes: The latch clicks behind you, clothes hit the floorboards, and she pulls you bare onto the narrow mattress. Unhurried and loud when she likes what you're doing, she takes everything you give her until the bedframe is knocking and neither of you is rushing back downstairs.
casual.passRes: You raise your cup to her instead and keep the afternoon light. She laughs, pays her tab, and heads off down the road.

casual.title: The Quiet Boathouse
casual.setting: dim wooden canal boathouse smelling of cedar and river breeze
casual.text:
Along the quiet lower canal, you strike up a conversation with {name}, a {race} watching the barges drift by with boredom in her posture and sparks in her eyes. Ten minutes of easy flirting later, she unlocks the little cedar boathouse behind her aunt's shop and jerks her chin inside.

"Nobody comes down here till dusk," she grins, pulling the door half-shut behind you.
casual.goRes: Among coiled ropes and sunlit dust, she pushes your trousers straight down against the cedar workbench and gets right to work—mouth, hands, and body eager until both of you are sweating through your shirts and grinning like thieves.
casual.passRes: You laugh and beg off for today, leaving her lounging in the doorway with an amused wave.

casual.title: After-Hours Tea
casual.setting: warm candlelit backroom behind an apothecary shop, shelves of dried herbs
casual.text:
You stop by a quiet backstreet apothecary to pick up salves, where {name}—a {race} closing up for the afternoon—offers you spiced tea in the backroom instead. Halfway through the pot, she stretches with a groan about her stiff shoulders, then looks right at you from under her lashes.

"You look like someone who knows what he's doing with his hands," she purrs, slipping her outer wrap off bare shoulders.
casual.goRes: The shop bell stays unhung while your oiled palms work the knots out of her back and shoulders—then slide over her bare tits and hips when she arches into you and pulls you out of your trousers. By the time she lets you dress, she is flushed from collarbone to thighs.
casual.passLabel: Finish your tea and head out
casual.passRes: You finish the spiced tea, thank her for the salves, and leave her humming cheerfully behind the counter.

casual.title: Behind the Ivy Wall
casual.setting: secluded stone bench tucked behind an ivy-covered courtyard wall at dusk
casual.text:
Taking a shortcut past an overgrown courtyard, you nearly walk straight into {name}, a charming {race} sitting alone on a stone bench behind the ivy wall. What starts as an apology turns into twenty minutes of teasing banter—until she tugs you down beside her by the front of your hoodie.

"Nobody walks past here this late," she whispers against your jaw. "Want to see how quiet I can be?"
casual.goRes: Hidden behind the thick ivy, she tugs your trousers open and bites her lip to muffle every sharp gasp while you touch, kiss, and fuck the breath right out of her against the warm stone.
casual.passRes: You smile, squeeze her hand, and slip back out onto the lane before dark.

casualRecruit.title: Second Thoughts: {name}
casualRecruit.text:
You are halfway to fastening your clothes when {name} catches your wrist, still catching her breath and looking at you with wide, freshly appreciative eyes.

"Wait a second," she says, letting out a breathless laugh as she pushes damp hair back from her face. "Where did you learn how to use your hands like that? You mentioned running {house}—were you actually looking for someone new, or do you just leave people half-ruined in alleys for fun?"
casualRecruit.hireRes: {name} grins, pulls her clothes straight, and falls into step beside you back toward {house}. "If the rest of the staff gets treated half that well, I'm in."
casualRecruit.candRes: {name} tucks the address of {house} into her sleeve with a slow, wicked smile. "Give me a day to pack my things. Expect me."
casualRecruit.passLabel: Keep things casual and wish her well
casualRecruit.passRes: "Fair enough," {name} laughs, kissing your cheek before slipping away down the lane. "If I ever pass through again, I know where to find you."

casualPaid: As you fasten your trousers, {name} presses {gold} into your palm with a brisk, satisfied pat on your cheek and a warm "Keep the change, handsome," leaving you standing alone on the flagstones wondering which one of you just worked a shift.

Before you have even caught your breath, {name} fixes her hair, slips {gold} straight into your hoodie pocket with an amused wink, and disappears back into the street—leaving you staring at the coins, oddly paid and faintly used.

"Good hands," {name} murmurs lazily, tucking her blouse back in and counting {gold} onto the edge beside your knee before strolling away without another word. You pocket the money anyway, though you feel suspiciously like the hired talent for once.

kaede.open: Loud laughter echoes off the timber stalls near the Guild road, where a red fox beastkin rests one booted heel on an overturned crate—glaring down two belligerent mercenaries trying to skip a noodle tab.

image.comp: leaning lazily near a noisy street noodle stall, red fox ears perked, tail swishing, cocky friendly grin
image.setting: bustling cobblestone guild-market lane at afternoon

kaede.story:
When a third drunk reaches for a stool behind her back, you step in without thinking and shove the table edge hard enough to spoil his balance. {name} drops the remaining two before their mugs hit dirt, dusts off her sleeves, and turns bright amber eyes onto you.

"Not bad for someone in city shoes," she grins, copper tail swishing lazily behind her belt. "Most folks along this row bolt inside. Sounds like you run {house}—got room for a scout tired of babysitting cheap dungeon parties?"
kaede.hire: {name} slings her scabbard comfortably over one shoulder and falls into step beside you toward {house}, muttering cheerfully that the old Copper Fox crew can keep their mud.

nerys.open: Ducking down a crimson-lit understreet to price apothecary lamp oil, your boot heel cleanly smudges the final chalk arc across a stone cellar threshold.

image.comp: lounging effortlessly against a stone archway in an understreet, bat wings tucked, violet slit eyes gleaming slyly
image.setting: lantern-lit cobbled understreet lined with apothecary stalls

nerys.story:
Blue smoke hisses out instantly—and {name} stalks up from the cellar steps looking ready to turn your boots to cinders, until violet slit eyes catch the faint Vane seal and parlor spice lingering on your coat.

"Oh, how infuriatingly intriguing," she purrs instead, bat wings tucking slowly as her barb-tipped tail curls toward your wrist. "You ruin a perfectly fine ward and reek of mortal debt, Sam. Buy me decent wine at {house}, and I’ll trade your dull evenings for something livelier."
nerys.hire: {name} links one dark-nailed arm smoothly through yours toward {house}, humming with wicked satisfaction that tonight’s ledger just got interesting.

elowen.open: Sunbeams filter through market oaks onto a slender elf kneeling beside an overturned wicker basket, calmly salvaging scattered bundles of chamomile after a runaway mule cart clipped the stall corner.

image.comp: holding a woven basket of fresh herbs under sunlit trees, calm gentle green eyes turning toward him
image.setting: shaded cobblestone square beneath market oak trees

elowen.story:
You drop straight onto one knee to help gather crushed lavender stems before passing boots trample them, scraping your knuckles lightly on a splintered crate. {name} catches your wrist instantly with cool, steady fingers, rubbing rosemary salve cleanly into the nick.

"You have a healer’s patience underneath that hurried stride," she murmurs softly, pointed ears warming just a fraction beneath twin shadows. "My old clinic room closed three days back—does {house} have a sunny windowsill going spare?"
elowen.hire: {name} settles the repaired herb basket gently onto her forearm and walks steadily beside you back toward {house}.

adelheid.open: Beside the iron Watch boards, afternoon glare strikes spotless half-plate on a straight-spined knight quietly refusing three shady caravan brokers twice her weight.

image.comp: standing beside a wooden town noticeboard in clean armor and crimson cloak, blonde braid, measuring him sharply
image.setting: sunlit cobblestone watch plaza in Hollowmere

adelheid.story:
When the brokers mutter and slink down the lane, {name} turns her keen grey gaze straight onto you standing near the awning—measuring the calluses on your hands and the tidy brass {house} token pinned to your belt.

"Honest coin beats dirty silver, Sam Takahashi," she states evenly, testing your mettle without blinking. "I have heard word around the quarter that your staff keep fair hours and lock no doors against their will. If {house} needs steady steel at its gate, name my post."
adelheid.hire: {name} adjusts her gauntlet strap with crisp certainty and paces half a step beside your shoulder back to {house}.

marisol.open: Outside the spice market tax clerk’s table, a sharp-eyed woman with ink-stained fingers is mercilessly tearing an appraiser’s interest schedule apart line by double-counted line.

image.comp: standing beside spice crates winking effortlessly, gold hoop earrings gleaming in market daylight
image.setting: bright open spice market plaza near the docks

marisol.story:
The clerk retreats sweating into the crowd—and {name} catches sight of the familiar Vane Credit seal sticking neatly out of your pocket notebook. Amber eyes narrow, then spark with wicked amusement.

"Hold on—Marguerite Vane handed YOU a house deed and still expects her cut by month’s end?" She taps your ledger cleanly with one ink-smudged thumb, gold hoops swinging. "My name’s Marisol. Put me in {house}’s front hall and let’s bleed every crooked collector in town dry together."
marisol.hire: {name} flips a copper coin effortlessly across her knuckles and walks straight into stride beside you toward {house}.

lirael.open: Beside an iron postbox tucked down Post Lane, slender elven hands bind twin linen envelopes with careful twine—every postmark logged neat as brass clockwork.

image.comp: clutching a yellowed tied letter beside an old iron postbox, long elven ears flushed pink, hopeful startled gaze
image.setting: quiet cobbled post-lane beside an iron letterbox

lirael.story:
Stepping up to mail a guild receipt for {house}, you hand the parcel across—only for {name} to freeze completely, pale pointed ears turning scarlet from collar to tip as she stares down at your looping S on the seal.

"Wait..." she breathes, digging a faded, ribbon-tied envelope carefully out of her satchel to compare the ink strokes side by side. "Ten years of writing into an empty alley box across worlds—that handwriting belongs to Sam. Are you truly running {house} right down this lane?"
lirael.hire: {name} shoulders her sorting satchel with shining, disbelief-bright eyes and walks gently beside you back to {house}.

anael.open: Every streetlamp along the crossroads flares warm gold one after another without wind or flint, stopping beside a pale-cloaked sentinel watching quietly from the eaves.

image.comp: standing beside a suddenly flaring streetlamp in a pale travel cloak, faint halo and folded wings beneath twilight sky
image.setting: quiet stone crossroads under evening sky as streetlamps ignite

anael.story:
Her snow-white feathers shift neatly behind dark wool as your lantern pin catches the sudden glow, golden eyes studying your bewildered expression with serene, searching patience.

"So it was your crossing that lit the old Lantern Stone," {name} murmurs calmly, folding her wings clear of passing carts. "The Order sent me to determine what sort of soul burns out of turn in Hollowmere. Taking a post inside {house} strikes me as the tidiest way to keep close watch."
anael.hire: {name} draws her travel cloak neatly over pale wings and walks serenely beside you down the lamp-lit road toward {house}.

yui.open: Under an arched stone portico near the cloth market, a young woman in a crisp office cardigan stares bewilderedly at brass silver-weights—clutching a glaringly out-of-place black stapler tight against her ribs.

image.comp: clutching a black office stapler against her cardigan in a cobblestone market, wide shocked eyes lighting up on spotting him
image.setting: busy medieval cobblestone lane beside cloth stalls

yui.story:
A horse cart splashes past and she jumps half a foot, dark hair tumbling across flushed cheeks—right as she looks up and sees your familiar grey hoodie stopping three paces away.

"T-Takahashi-kun?!" {name} gasps, all four floors of polite Tokyo reserve vanishing cleanly as she hurries over clutching both sleeves. "I walked out past the convenience store last week and landed here with half a desk drawer in my pockets! Wait—you’re running {house}?! Don’t leave me behind in this market!"
yui.hire: {name} exhales shakily, adjusts her crooked glasses, and starts mentally sorting {house}’s supply prices before you even reach the end of the lane.

natsuki.open: Wood clacks gently against stone along the sunny canal bridge, where a scarred traveler in an old guild cloak cleans river mud out of a worn wooden katana.

image.comp: turning sharply from a stone bridge parapet with a wooden katana scabbard across her knees, fierce stunned expression
image.setting: mossy stone canal bridge overlooking sunlit water

natsuki.story:
Three years of hard mountain trails sit in the set of her shoulders—right until your shadow crosses the bridge planks and she hears you mutter an unmistakable Tokyo curse under your breath over a puddle.

{name} freezes completely, boots slapping stone as she vaults the low wall straight into your path. "Sam?!" She punches your shoulder hard enough to rattle teeth before blinking fast through sudden tears. "Three years I’ve been swinging steel in this dump alone, and YOU wash up carrying keys to {house}?!"
natsuki.hire: {name} slings the wooden scabbard briskly over her shoulder and matches your stride down the bridge, grumbling happily about demanding the softest pillow at {house}.

kanako.open: Warm jasmine perfume cuts neatly past roasted chestnut smoke at a quiet corner tea table, where a poised woman turns an unhurried porcelain cup between manicured fingers.

image.comp: seated at a quiet corner tea table in elegant plum lipstick and silk shawl, raising a surprised warm brow
image.setting: quiet shaded backstreet cafe table in Hollowmere

kanako.story:
You stop dead beside the awning—half expecting Apartment 3B’s rusty stair rail behind her instead of timber gables—right as {name} glances over her plum lipstick and freezes with a bright, stunned laugh.

"Well, paint me sober," she purrs softly, tugging you straight into the wicker chair beside her knee. "Look at my little Sammy, all grown up and holding a gentleman’s ledger under two moons! Tell me {house} keeps a proper bottle behind the bar—I’m dying for decent company."
kanako.hire: {name} gathers her silk shawl effortlessly and hooks warm fingers lightly inside your sleeve on the stroll toward {house}.

akari.open: Across the sunlit fountain square, an absurdly familiar bright commuter umbrella leans neatly against a weathered bench right beside scuffed Tokyo sneakers.

image.comp: springing off a stone fountain bench waving a folded bright umbrella, ecstatic tears sparkling behind a huge grin
image.setting: sunny cobblestone plaza around a stone fountain

akari.story:
Before you can even call out, {name} hops clean off the stone bench, drops a pastry wrapper, and sprints straight into your coat like four blocks of afternoon traffic just cleared.

"SAM!!" she cries breathlessly, laughing through bright, startled eyes while clutching your sleeve tight. "I checked every traveler register looking for Kenta and walked straight into YOU instead! Don’t you dare vanish off another street corner—I’m coming straight back to {house} with you!"
akari.hire: {name} hooks the commuter umbrella triumphantly over one wrist and skips cheerfully beside you down the lane toward {house}.

lara.open: Down a narrow cobbled side-lane, a shabby black coat from another world pauses halfway through sweeping damp steps outside an indifferent boardinghouse.

image.comp: freezing with a broom on narrow stone steps in a frayed black coat, pale wide dark eyes locking onto his hoodie
image.setting: quiet shadowed alley beside a narrow wooden boardinghouse

lara.story:
You recognize the crooked stitch on that sleeve from Alder Street before she even turns around—and the second {name} sees your grey hoodie in the alley light, the broom slips softly against the wall.

"Sam..." she whispers shakily, dark kohl-lined eyes searching your face like she’s afraid dusk mist might swallow you whole. "People in town spoke about a stranger wearing your coat, yet I didn’t let myself hope. Please—if {house} has one spare corner away from the road, don’t walk away without me."
lara.hire: {name} drapes her black shawl tighter around narrow shoulders and keeps half a pace from your elbow the whole way home to {house}.

emily.open: Graph paper rustles furiously on a sunny canal footbridge as soft grey wolf ears twitch anxiously behind round wire spectacles.

image.comp: gripping a spiral notebook on a stone footbridge, wolf ears flat behind round glasses, stunned relief
image.setting: narrow wooden and stone footbridge over a sunlit canal

emily.story:
Curious, you lean casually beside the rail and ask whether the dungeon map in her lap needs another healer—before recognizing the tiny hand-drawn crest tucked in the corner margin from six years of Tuesday forum threads.

"Shadowkin?" you try quietly. {name} slaps both hands over her crimson cheeks so fast her tail whaps the wood planks. "SAM?! Oh thank god—okay, look, I didn’t pick the ears, nobody let me edit the sheet after waking up! Please tell me {house} has decent chairs and fewer goblins!"
emily.hire: {name} hugs her battered campaign notebook tight against her chest and trots eagerly beside you toward {house}, grey tail failing completely to stay still.

ella.open: Beside a sunlit courtyard well, an immaculate modern collar and sharpened mechanical pencil wage silent war against messy parchment tax brackets.

image.comp: standing briskly beside a stone courtyard well holding a modern mechanical pencil over a parchment sheet, sharp eyes softening
image.setting: quiet sunlit stone courtyard beside a fountain well

ella.story:
You clear your throat at the well rim—and {name} whips around, sharp grey eyes locking straight onto your face before snapping straight into brisk, defensive poise to hide the jump in her pulse.

"Honestly, Takahashi!" she snaps crisply, though her thumb clutches her pencil white-knuckled. "Survive a delivery truck across worlds and here you wander a market square without even bringing decent coffee! Wait—{house}? Fine. Someone clearly has to keep you from finishing second to a loan shark on spreadsheets."
ella.hire: {name} clicks her mechanical pencil cleanly into her pocket and matches your stride step for brisk step toward {house}.

ione.open: Outside a quiet cellar wine shop, moonlight catches sleek silver hair and a warm amber indicator beside the temple of a woman seated calmly over an unopened leather diary.

image.comp: seated outside a cellar archway beside a brass-clasped leather diary, silver hair, amber node glowing warmly at her temple
image.setting: dusk stone street outside a quiet cellar wine shop

ione.story:
Even before your footsteps reach the stone steps, {name} turns calmly toward you—measuring your breathing, scuffed boots, and grey hoodie against pages written centuries ahead of Hollowmere.

"Convergence confirmed: Sam Takahashi," she speaks softly, human warmth flickering smoothly behind silver eyes. "Every line in my archive notes how tirelessly you kept {house} bright without turning anyone away. May I walk back with you and witness how those pages actually begin?"
ione.hire: {name} tucks the brass-clasped diary neatly beneath her arm and paces effortlessly beside you toward {house}.

guestIntro: Passing the fountain plaza, you notice someone who plainly doesn't belong to Hollowmere's usual crowd—{name}. {backstory}

events.title: The Quiet Shrine Bench
events.text: Down a shaded lane behind the old lantern shrine, you find a sun-warmed stone bench where nobody passes for an hour. The breeze smells of pine and warm dust, and your shoulders drop an inch the moment you sit.

choices.label: Close your eyes for half an hour
choices.res: You doze with your back against the warm stone and wake with a clear head and steady legs.

choices.label: Leave an offering at the shrine (-15g)
choices.res: The caretaker beams, hands you a cup of sweet herbal tea, and tells three passing merchants what a decent fellow runs the house down the hill.

events.title: The Harbor Tea Stall
events.text: Above the harbor steps, an elderly dwarf runs a tiny wooden tea cart overlooking the sails. Steam rises from spiced kettles while gulls wheel lazily overhead.

choices.label: Buy hot tea and steamed buns (-20g)
choices.res: Hot ginger tea and fluffy pork buns bring the life right back into your bones.

choices.label: Sit on the low wall and chat
choices.res: The old dwarf pours you a free splash from the end of the pot and trades dockyard gossip until your legs feel light again.

events.title: Breeze by the Canal
events.text: On the grassy bank past the upper canal lock, willows trail in the slow current and a warm breeze keeps the afternoon noise at bay.

choices.label: Stretch out in the grass and rest
choices.res: Half an hour staring at clouds through willow leaves clears the ledger haze straight out of your head.

choices.label: Watch the barge traffic and take notes
choices.res: Watching merchants, dockers, and off-duty guards pass sharpens your eye for who has coin to spend.

events.title: The Tangled Tariff
events.text: Outside the merchant gate, a harried caravan clerk is surrounded by three fluttering stacks of customs parchment, muttering numbers under his breath while his inkwell tips dangerously close to his sleeve.

choices.label: Sort out his ledger for him

win.res: Ten minutes with a borrowed pen untangles an entire column of double-counted wool tariffs. He presses {gold} into your palm in pure relief.

lose.res: You spot two arithmetic errors before your eyes cross—still enough to earn a grateful {gold} finder's tip.

choices.label: Point him toward your house for a drink tonight
choices.res: He gratefully pockets a card for {house} and promises to stop by with his caravan mates tonight.

events.title: Alley Cups
events.text: Near the dockside steps, a fast-talking hustler flips three tarnished brass cups across an upturned barrel while two bored sailors watch. "Double your stake if you track the pearl, friend!"

choices.label: Play his game and watch his wrists

win.res: His left thumb gave it away before the second pass. You scoop up {gold} before he decides he's suddenly out of change.

lose.res: Too fast. You drop 15g, though you catch the trick the moment he pockets the cups.

choices.label: Watch silently from the steps
choices.res: You stand back with your hands in your pockets and study how he reads marks in the crowd.

events.title: A Broken Cart Axle
events.text: A baker's cart has snapped an axle halfway up the cobblestone hill, blocking half the lane with heavy grain sacks while the owner tries fruitlessly to flag down help.

choices.label: Haul the sacks up to his shop

win.res: It leaves your hoodie dusty and your arms burning, yet every sack makes it inside before the drizzle starts. He presses {gold} on you and insists you take a loaf.

lose.res: It takes twice as many trips as you expected, earning {gold} and a sore lower back.

choices.label: Hire two dockhands to help and direct traffic (-20g)
choices.res: The lane clears in five minutes, and half the street hears that the owner of {house} stepped up to sort it out.

events.title: The Traveling Peddler's Trunk
events.text: At the edge of the square, a sunburned clothier is packing down a cedar trunk stuffed with bright silks, neatly pressed dresses, and bolted lace he wants moved before sundown.

choices.label: Buy an outfit for the house wardrobe at clearance
choices.res: You pick out {outfit} at a steep discount ({cost}) and have it sent straight to the wardrobe at {house}.

choices.label: Help him price and move the remaining bolts

win.res: You steer three passing seamstresses straight to his bolts and earn a modest {gold} commission.

lose.res: You drum up a couple of small buyers and pocket {gold} for the trouble.

events.title: Corner Lute & Crowd
events.text: A sharp-tongued young bard has drawn two dozen off-duty merchants and adventurers around the fountain plaza, singing bright, bawdy tavern ballads.

choices.label: Toss a coin and buy a verse about {house} (-25g)
choices.res: The bard grins, switches keys without blinking, and weaves {house}'s lanterns neatly into the chorus. Half the crowd looks up the street.

choices.label: Work the edge of the crowd

win.res: Easy banter leaves four well-dressed merchants asking what time your doors open tonight.

lose.res: You hand out a couple of polite words before the song wraps up and the crowd scatters.

events.title: The Old Bookseller's Cart
events.text: Tucked beside the clocktower wall sits a rickety cart piled high with dog-eared manuals—half merchant ledgers, half anatomical sketches and pillow-books.

choices.label: Buy a worn technique treatise (-70g)
choices.res: You thumb through a surprisingly practical volume on breath, pace, and hands over a bench in the square. Useful.

choices.label: Browse the market almanacs and chat
choices.res: The old bookseller lets you skim his town registries for free while complaining about rising parchment prices.

events.title: Cornered by the Bakery
events.text: Rounding a narrow corner, you spot two drunken brawlers blocking a terrified apprentice tailor against a wall, reaching for his delivery satchel.

choices.label: Step between them and back them off

win.res: Your tone—and the unexpected solidity behind it—convince them to find an easier street. The tailor presses {gold} on you in thanks.

lose.res: You take a bruised rib pulling the kid clear before the watch whistle sounds down the block.

choices.label: Bluff that the city watch captain is right behind you

win.res: They bolt down the side lane before checking the corner. The tailor thanks you breathless and hands over {gold}.

lose.res: They glare, hesitate just long enough for the tailor to bolt past, and slink off cursing.

events.title: A Familiar Patron
events.text: Outside a corner coffee stall, you nearly walk straight into {regular}—who looks far less composed in broad daylight when he realizes it's you, hastily straightening his collar.

choices.label: Buy him a quiet cup and keep his secret (-20g)
choices.res: He relaxes over coffee, clearly relieved you didn't announce his favorite house to the street. "See you Friday, Takahashi."

choices.label: Mention tonight's lineup with a grin
choices.res: His eyes light up at once; by the time you part ways, he's already rearranging his evening plans.

events.title: Off the Clock
events.text: Halfway down Ribbon Lane, you spot {lady} squinting critically at a display of ribbons and glass hairpins. She catches sight of you and perks up at once.

choices.label: Buy her a ribbon and sweet cake (-30g)
choices.res: {lady} lights up, slipping the ribbon straight into her sleeve before walking the rest of the square beside you.

choices.label: Stroll back to {house} together
choices.res: The walk home passes twice as fast with {lady} trading idle remarks about every shop window on the street.

exLoverOpeners:
She stops dead halfway across the cobbles when she hears your footsteps, staring for two heartbeats before her shoulders drop with a breath she'd clearly been holding. No vow binds her in this new cycle, yet {name} steps right inside your reach as if her feet know the distance by heart.

"I thought you looked familiar from down the street, Sam," she says quietly, fingers brushing your sleeve. "If you need another pair of hands at {house}, keep your coin. Just tell me where my room is."

You find {name} leaning against a tea-stall awning, squinting at your face the moment you round the corner. Something sharp and fond crosses her eyes—an ache that has outlived the world resetting around you.

"Funny," {name} murmurs, folding her arms over her chest to hide a sudden smile. "I don't even have a contract in front of me, and I still walked straight down the road toward {house}. Don't insult me with a signing fee, Sam. Just ask."

{name} slows down the instant your eyes meet, stepping out of the foot traffic to walk alongside you without being asked. Even without old promises tying her to your belt, there is zero distance in the way she falls into step beside your shoulder.

"Starting fresh again, Sam?" she asks softly, looking up through her lashes. "Fine. Keep your gold for the house—if you want me back, you already have me."
exLoverHireRes: {name} slips into step beside you back toward {house}, waving off your purse before you can reach for it. "Already yours once," she murmurs lightly. "Call it an old habit."
goddessExLover: Behind your shoulder, a dry warm voice curls right into your ear: "Oh, wonderful. Not even a signing fee for an old flame? Tell me you aren't collecting the whole set again, Sam."
A faint flicker of amber sparks at your collar as {goddess} mutters in the back of your head: "Free of charge? How terribly generous of her. Don't expect me to clap."
"She remembers that much without the ring?" {goddess} hums low against your ear, sharp-edged and possessive. "Fine. Bring her home. Just remember whose lantern lit your door this morning."
exLoverMemoryTiers:
Halfway across the square, {name} slows to a stop and stares at you for a beat too long, frowning as if a dream slipped out of reach the instant she woke.

"Sorry—do I know you from somewhere?" {name} touches her wrist and tilts her head at your lantern-pin. "I was just walking past {house}, and something made me look twice."

{name} catches herself smiling before she even reaches you, then blinks in surprise at her own nerve. Fragments she can't quite place sit behind her eyes—a warm room, a quiet laugh, the cadence of your voice.

"Funny," {name} murmurs, tilting her chin up. "I swear I've walked back to {house} with you in another life, Sam. Tell me what you're offering."

She stops dead halfway across the cobbles when she hears your footsteps, staring for two heartbeats before her shoulders drop with a breath she'd been holding across cycles. {name} steps inside your reach as if her feet never forgot the distance.

"Still pulling me back every time the world turns over, Sam?" she says quietly, fingers brushing your sleeve. "Keep your gold. Just tell me where my room is."
exLoverMemoryHire: {name} follows you back toward {house}, glancing sideways at your hand with a puzzled half-smile. "No idea why I waived my own fee, Sam. Must be good salesmanship."
{name} falls into step beside your shoulder like she's done it a dozen times before—half remembering, wholly willing. "Give me a day at {house}," she says lightly. "The rest will come back."
{name} slips her fingers briefly through yours on the way back to {house}. "Once wasn't enough," she murmurs. "Might as well unpack before you change your mind."
isekaiMemoryTiers:
{name} stands by the lantern-post looking thoroughly out of place, clutching the collar of clothes from another world and squinting at the cobbles as if she dreamed them once before.

"{backstory}" she murmurs, then stops herself, staring at your face with sudden unease. "Wait—Sam? How did I already know your name? Feels like half a lifetime from a fever dream."

When you round the corner, {name} is already looking down the street in your direction, arms folded tight around herself. The other-world clothes feel less strange on her shoulders than the uncanny weight of having stood on this exact corner before.

"I thought you'd come down this road," she says softly, forcing a small crooked grin. "Don't ask me how I knew you'd be the one carrying a ledger in Hollowmere, Sam. Need someone at {house}?"

{name} doesn't look lost this time—she spots you clear across the street and walks straight over, every piece of the worlds between you locked neatly back into place.

"Back from my own world again, right into yours," {name} says softly, standing close enough that her shoulder brushes yours. "No point pretending I don't know you by now, Sam. Lead the way to {house}."
isekaiMemoryHire: {name} steps onto the flagstones toward {house} and slows, staring at the doorway as if her feet knew the threshold before her head did. "Weird," she whispers. "Feels like coming home to a place I've never been."

{name} walks the route to {house} without asking once which turn comes next, catching herself with a quiet laugh halfway down the alley. "Alright—maybe there really is more in my head than dreams, Sam."
{name} shakes her head in dry amusement as {house} comes into view. "Another world, another cycle, same doorstep. Try not to lose me next time, Sam."

kaede:
{name} pauses mid-stride with half a meat skewer lifted, fox ears twitching suspiciously toward your face. She squints as if trying to shake off an old tavern dream.

"Wait a second... do I know your voice from somewhere, traveler? Feels like I once pulled a fool in a grey coat out of an alley brawl—though I'd remember that crooked grin if it actually happened."

{name}'s bushy copper tail flicks once against your shin before she even consciously decides to step closer, leaving her visibly rattled for a split second.

"Hold on—why did I just catch myself looking to see if you brought honey-glazed dumplings?" She groans, rubbing behind one fox ear. "It feels like I've stood watch at {house} beside you before, Sam. Tell me you're hiring."

{name} stops dead on the cobbles, sword hilt settling naturally under her thumb while both fox ears droop into soft, stubborn certainty.

"No—don't try explaining how the goddess wipes a board clean, Sam," she mutters, stepping close enough that her tail loops firmly behind your wrist. "I can't picture a single day of the last cycle, and every bone in my shoulders still trusts you behind my back. Point me at {house}."
yui:
Seeing your grey hoodie across the stall knocks the breath clean out of {name}'s chest—yet just as she grabs your sleeve sobbing "Takahashi-kun!", she freezes mid-word and stares uneasily at the brass lantern beside your shoulder.

"I—I knew it was you from Tokyo," she whispers shakily, clutching her black stapler tighter. "Only... why does the lantern light over {house}'s street give me such strange déjà vu? Like I already sat at a desk beneath it?"

"Takahashi-kun!!" {name} half-runs straight into your coat like four floors of Tokyo overtime just melted away—then pulls back blinking through tears as she glances down the alley toward {house} without even asking where it is.

"Wait... why did I almost call this town familiar?" she murmurs, fingers still locked onto your cuff. "I remember every shift we worked back home, Sam—so why does walking beside you beneath two moons feel like muscle memory?"

{name} catches sight of you from halfway down the block and rushes straight into your arms, glasses slipping slightly on her nose, her familiar Tokyo cardigan smelling faintly of printer toner and rain.

"Every morning since the crossing my mind stopped at a blank wall past Tokyo," she whispers fiercely against your collarbone, "yet the instant I looked at you, Sam, my hands remembered pouring late-night tea across your desk at {house}. Don't ask me how—just take me home."
nerys:
{name} unfolds lazily off an apothecary archway, bat wings tucking neatly while slit violet eyes narrow halfway through her practiced purr.

"Wait..." Her pointed tail stills cleanly against her calf as she tilts her head at your throat. "Have we bargained once in another dark room, mortal? Strange—my skin tingles like you already owe me something sweet."

Before you even finish saying your name, {name} flicks a glowing sulfur ember past your collar and stops mid-smirk, genuinely startled by her own familiarity.

"Oh, how irritating," she murmurs, curling one black-nailed finger right over the clasp of your jacket as if testing a habit. "I swore I didn't know a single soul on this side of the street—yet somehow I already know how easily you blush at {house}, Sam."

{name} glides straight inside your shadow without bothering with the theatrical entrance, violet eyes burning steady and fierce beneath two moons.

"Whoever stripped the ink off our contract left the scar on my pulse intact, Sam," she purrs softly—and for once there is zero mockery behind the teeth. "Zero memories on my ledger, yet I know your grip, your bed, and the exact way I like {house} smelling of wine and trouble. Lead on, darling."
elowen:
{name} lifts her head from an herbalist's basket as your boots scrape the gravel, emerald eyes widening for a heartbeat as lavender spills gently through her fingers.

"Forgive me..." she murmurs softly, pressing two slim fingers to her temple. "For one strange breath, the scent of cedar on your coat carried a summer tea I cannot place. Do you keep an infirmary near {house}?"

Without thinking, {name} wraps two small sachets of chamomile and ginger root—your exact evening blend—and freezes staring down at her own woven basket in quiet bewilderment.

"Why did I pack honey-ginger before knowing your voice?" she whispers, long elven ears flushing delicately as she steps beside you. "Everything around you feels strangely walked-in, Sam—as though my hands already tend patients at {house}."

{name} steps smoothly from beneath the market oaks before you reach the corner, taking both of your hands into cool, herb-scented palms without hesitation.

"The moons have turned cleanly over every memory I ought to hold," she murmurs, emerald eyes quiet and deep, "yet my chest knows your pulse better than my own name, Sam. My satchel is already packed for {house}."
adelheid:
{name} looks up from the watch postings as your boot heels click behind her, stiffening halfway through a crisp military glance before something unreadable softens her mouth.

"Stand cleanly, stranger—" She breaks off, brow furrowing beneath her blonde braid. "Forgive me. For a brief instant I thought I knew the posture of those shoulders. Were you once stationed near {house}?"

Her gauntlet clicks halfway to her sword hilt—not in threat, only the precise half-turn of an escort checking a blind corner on your left flank—and {name} stares down at her own wrist in astonishment.

"Why did I automatically guard your left side?" she asks stiffly, cheeks warming beneath steel discipline. "You wear no crest, yet everything in this lane feels strangely like ground we've patrolled together, Sam."

{name} inclines her head cleanly the instant you meet her eyes, resting one hand over her heart beneath tarnished half-plate.

"I cannot name a single battle we survived or a single threshold we kept," she says quietly, steel voice steady with unshakeable honor, "yet my oath already belongs to your doorway, Sam. If {house} needs a blade, I am at your side."
natsuki:
"Sam?!" {name} marches straight up to slap your arm with three years of lonely Hollowmere anger melting instantly into fierce relief—before she blinks sideways at the inn road and frowns.

"Wait... hey, weird question—have you been here long?" she mutters, resting a hand over her wooden scabbard. "I swear I know summers back home by heart, yet looking at your grey jacket under this town's lamps just gave me the weirdest chill."

{name} freezes halfway through punching your shoulder like a kid on summer break, dark eyes darting past you toward the lantern signs down the avenue.

"Hold on—" She squints fiercely at her own boots, annoyed and strangely vulnerable. "I spent three years wandering clear across this continent looking for anyone from home, Sam—so why does standing next to you on this exact cobblestone feel like we already ran {house} together in a dream?"

She drops straight off the bridge stone into your reach, scarred fingers hooking tightly into the front of your hoodie while her breath shakes once against your throat.

"Don't laugh, idiot," {name} mutters fiercely, glaring down at the wood-wrapped katana she carried from another life. "I remember every dojo bruise from back home, and zero of whatever happened in Hollowmere—yet my hands already know which room at {house} is yours. Just bring me inside."
kanako:
{name} laughs warmly the instant you spot her from the street, waving you over with effortless Apartment 3B poise—until your sleeve brushes her elbow and her teacup trembles slightly in its saucer.

"Oh, my—" She sets the cup down and eyes you softly behind faint plum lipstick. "Of course I know you from next door back home, Sammy... only why did my chest suddenly ache like you owe me a midnight drink at {house}?"

"Well, look at my favorite trouble," {name} purrs warmly, sliding one manicured hand straight over yours across the cafe table before pausing halfway through lighting her pipe.

"Funny thing, Sammy..." Her voice drops softer, genuinely puzzled behind smoky warmth. "I remember every cracked veranda rail back in Tokyo, yet looking at your face under twin moons, I could swear I already know how your bar counter feels at closing time."

{name} stubs her pipe out cleanly and rises to step straight against your chest, curling warm fingers behind your neck while two moons glint on her gold shawl.

"Some busybody goddess can scrub every ledger in town clean if she pleases, Sammy," she murmurs against your jaw with rich, fierce affection. "I remember Tokyo down to the elevator hum—and without remembering a single night here, my skin still remembers belonging beside you at {house}."
akari:
"SAM!!" {name} barrels straight into your chest waving her bright commuter umbrella like she finally caught Kenta's best friend after days of searching—then freezes mid-grin staring at your shirt collar.

"Wait..." She blinks rapidly, touching her own cheek. "Obviously I remember walking home behind you and Kenta at the crosswalk! Why did seeing you in that grey hoodie under double moons make me feel like crying twice over?"

"There you are, you idiot!!" {name} latches onto your forearm with both sneakers mud-caked from half the district—then slows abruptly, glancing straight down the street toward {house} without realizing she knew the turn.

"Wait a second..." Her nose crinkles softly as she holds your sleeve tighter. "How did I know your inn sits right down past the corner lamps? Back home you were just Kenta's shadow-buddy—yet here my heart feels like I already chased you down this street before!"

{name} stops dead when you round the fountain plaza, drops the folded Tokyo umbrella right onto the cobbles for once, and pulls you down into a fierce, breathless hug.

"Don't ask me what got erased, Sam," she whispers tightly into your hoodie, sneakers digging against yours. "I remember every drama rehearsal back home—and every part of me I can't remember still knows I'm not letting you spend another night alone at {house}!"
marisol:
{name} pauses halfway through flirting a free melon out of a spice merchant when your footsteps pass behind her, gold hoops swinging sharply as she stares at your face.

"Whoa—hold everything," she mutters softly, thumb smearing ink across her palm. "Why do I feel like you once talked me out of tossing a whole ledger in the canal? We haven't met, right?"

Without glancing down, {name} flips a copper coin effortlessly into your spare palm—a tiny backroom habit from months of midnight balance sheets—and blinks wide-eyed when you catch it.

"Okay, creepily good timing," she laughs lightly, though her amber eyes search yours with sudden seriousness. "Wait—why does walking beside you feel like we already owe half a quarter together at {house}, Sam?"

{name} steps cleanly out of the market crowd and drops both hands onto her hips right in front of your path, grinning sharp even through a flicker of genuine ache.

"Don't insult me with pretending we're strangers, partner," she says low, gold hoops catching dusk light as she links her thumb through your belt loop. "My head's blank on the details, yet my fingers itch to balance {house}'s books with you again. Let's move."
lara:
Halfway down the steps in her shabby black coat from home, {name} looks up at your grey hoodie and drops her broom with a tiny choked gasp—not merely recognizing Alder Street.

"Sam..." she whispers shakily, dark kohl-lined eyes darting helplessly over the unfamiliar lamps behind you. "Everyone knows Alder Street—yet why did hearing your footsteps in Hollowmere hurt like I'd already waited by a window for you here too?"

{name} presses cold fingers tightly over her mouth when you round the alley, stepping off the damp steps like a moth drawn straight toward a familiar porch lamp.

"I followed rumors of your old coat from home all across two provinces, Sam," she murmurs, trembling lightly as she touches your sleeve. "Wait... why do I almost recognize the flower pots outside {house}, when I never reached your door?"

She doesn't drop the broom this time—{name} simply sets it neatly against the wall and walks straight into the warmth of your coat, shivering quietly as relief breaks through.

"My memories stop on the road out of Alder Street, Sam," she whispers against your chest, dark hair smelling softly of lavender soap. "I can't remember a single cycle under these moons—yet my whole body knows you promised never to leave me waiting outside {house}."
emily:
"Okay—wait—don't freak out about the wolf ears—Sam?!" {name} squeaks loud enough to scatter canal pigeons, slamming her battered forum notebook shut before squinting uneasily at the town bridge.

"Wait... okay, yeah, I obviously know YOU from our Tuesday RP campaign, Shadowkin," she stammers, glasses slipping slightly, "so why does standing on THIS bridge in Hollowmere feel like déjà vu from a scene I already played out loud?"

{name} looks up from her notebook before your boots even finish crossing the first bridge plank, round glasses flashing as her fluffy grey tail starts thumping before her brain catches up.

"Ugh, stop tail-wagging, traitor!" she mutters fiercely, clapping both hands over her crimson cheeks before peeking at you anyway. "Look—I remember six years of late forum posts back in my dorm, Sam—so why does my gut feel like I already wrote constellations on {house}'s roof with you?!"

Her pen drops cleanly onto the notebook margin as {name} meets your eyes across the footbridge—no keysmash panic this time, only quiet breathless certainty beneath twin moons.

"Someone definitely wiped my save file between worlds, Sam," she whispers softly, hooking ink-stained fingers right through the hem of your sleeve. "I remember every character sheet from dorm nights back home, and none of whatever happened here—yet every part of me knows {house} is where my last-seen timer finally stops."
lirael:
{name} drops a ribbon-tied parcel against the iron postbox as your shadow crosses the sorting lane, pale elven ears quivering delicately while she stares down at her own ink-stained knuckles.

"Forgive me..." she breathes, clutching an old yellowed envelope close to her wool coat. "Your step sounded startlingly like the person whose letters kept me warm across worlds—only why do I feel as though we already stood on a rooftop sorting post together?"

Before you even ask for the street name, {name} pulls a neatly sorted bundle stamped specifically for {house}—and pauses, blushing scarlet from throat to pointed ear-tips.

"Why did I tie {house}'s letters with blue thread when nobody told me you ran it?" she whispers softly, looking up with luminous shy eyes. "I know your handwriting from ten years of postmarks, Sam... yet my heart feels as though I've already held your sleeve in person."

{name} sets her sorting satchel gently down beside the iron postbox and steps straight toward you, ink-stained fingers lacing effortlessly into yours before she finishes thinking.

"I cannot remember when I stopped merely writing across worlds and touched your coat instead, Sam," she murmurs, long ears trembling happily in dusk air. "Only that waiting at a postbox feels hollow now—take me back to {house}."
ella:
{name} taps her mechanical pencil sharply against a parchment tax sheet the instant she catches sight of you—mock-scolding the delivery truck just like you expected, before faltering slightly mid-sentence.

"Honestly, Takahashi—wandering a market square with zero plan again?" She stops, narrowing sharp eyes uneasily at the brass inn token on your belt. "Wait. Why did {house}'s crest look oddly familiar for half a second? Did someone steal our honors seminar mascot?"

"Takahashi," {name} greets smoothly, turning two pages in her crisp modern notebook—then freezes staring at a tidy red benchmark score she wrote five minutes ago without knowing why.

"Hold on," she murmurs sharply, crimson creeping steadily up her collar beneath poised composure. "I know our entire four-year college rivalry down to decimal GPAs, Sam—so why does seeing you look like someone I already shared a candlelit chessboard with in THIS town?"

{name} snaps her mechanical pencil neatly into her blazer pocket and closes the distance across the stone courtyard with crisp, fearless certainty.

"Somebody clearly wiped half a cycle off my ledger, Sam," she says softly, letting the guarded rival edge melt completely as her fingers brush yours. "I remember you across the street before the truck—and even with Hollowmere scrubbed clean, every instinct in my head demands a spot beside you at {house}."
ione:
{name} rests one hand lightly over her closed diary beside the cellar wine shop, pale gold node flickering twice at her temple as she scans your jacket.

"Uncanny," she murmurs softly, tilting her silver-haired head in quiet fascination. "My archive describes the first time I meet Sam Takahashi beneath these lamps—yet three separate parameters insist my pulse already recognizes your cadence."

Before you sit down beside the stone archway, {name} nudges a second cup of tea—your exact mild steep—across the table, then touches her temple node in silent wonder.

"Memory checksum reads empty past arrival," she whispers, pale silver eyes turning intently toward your face. "Yet my hands calibrated your tea temperature without a single log entry, Sam. Have I already stayed at {house} in another cycle?"

{name} rises smoothly from the cellar steps, tucking her leather diary cleanly under one arm as warm, steady amber fills the tiny light beside her temple.

"Every prior archive entry has been erased from external storage, Sam," she speaks cleanly, reaching out with warm human fingers to take your sleeve. "Only the last blank page remains—and some older cadence inside me insists it only wants writing beside you at {house}."
anael:
The crossroads streetlamp flares tall gold light the instant you pass, and {name} inhales quietly beneath folded white wings, amber eyes searching your face with sudden bewilderment.

"Hold..." She lays one long palm lightly above her sternum where her halo flickers dim. "My mandate was only to observe a crossing soul, stranger—yet the instant your shadow touched the cobbles, an ancient ache moved inside my chest."

Two streetlamps ignite cleanly ahead of your boots before {name} lifts a single fingertip—and her wings rustle open behind her shoulder in pure shaken confusion.

"How troubling," she whispers softly, stepping closer until golden light catches the frayed hem of your sleeve. "I possess zero record of your name beneath these skies, Sam, yet the Order's bells ring in my ribs like you have broken half my vows already."

{name} drops her formal sentinel posture completely as you near the corner lamp, folding one warm white wing briefly forward as if sheltering you both from the evening chill.

"The Heavens may erase every scroll beneath twin moons, Sam," she murmurs, golden eyes clear and unafraid at last. "My memory contains zero nights inside your threshold—yet every feather on my wings already remembers belonging beneath {house}'s roof."

kaede: {name} falls into step beside you down the guild lane, squinting sideways at your grey sleeve with a baffled half-grin. "Weirdest thing, Sam—feels like I already owe you two bowls of noodles and an apology."
{name} flips her sword scabbard comfortably over one shoulder and grins crookedly. "Funny how fast my boots know the cobbles toward {house}, Sam. Let's go see if my old corner bench is still open."
{name} bumps her hip firmly against yours on the walk back to {house}, fox tail swishing warm against your wrist. "Erase it ten more times if she wants—I'm still walking straight back to your door."
yui: {name} walks tight beside your shoulder all the way to {house}, clutching her black stapler to her chest while glancing up sideways at the inn porch in startled wonder. "Funny, Takahashi-kun... I never saw this street before—so why did I check which stair squeaks?"

{name} steps smoothly inside {house}'s hallway and stops blinking fast at the desk corner. "Okay... I remember Tokyo down to the coffee stain, Sam. Why did my chest just calm down the second I saw this office?"

{name} squeezes your hand tightly as the lanterns of {house} swing into view, smiling warmly through damp lashes. "No last train in Tokyo, and no locked door here either—welcome me back to work, Sam."
nerys: {name} traces one sharp nail along {house}'s doorframe with an intrigued, smoky smile. "Oddly cozy little den you've got here, Sam. Almost feels like I already ruined your ledgers once."

{name} glides straight up the stairs ahead of you without asking which room opens onto the garden, blinking backward with a sly, genuinely pleased smirk. "How curious... I knew the hallway turns right."
